variants.headline: People leave the colony on the ship
variants.sub: The ship has taken away young adults with no work and families with no home.
variants.body:
The ship in port has taken {left} people away from the colony: young adults with no work and families with no home. For {target}, the departure raises a direct question about the conditions of belonging, rather than a simple argument over whether a smaller population is a good or bad headline.

Labour's question is not whether a person ought to love the colony enough to endure anything. Labour finds the stewardship of {target} wanting; ordinary people deserve a more responsible standard of conduct.

variants.headline: Departure follows a lack of work and homes
variants.sub: Young adults lacking work and families lacking homes have departed the colony aboard the ship.
variants.body:
Young adults without work and families without homes have left on the ship. The number departing is {left}. Readers considering {target} should keep those stated circumstances in view, without turning the departure into an invented account of where people will go or whether they hope to return.

Labour's question is not whether a person ought to love the colony enough to endure anything. Labour finds the stewardship of {target} wanting; ordinary people deserve a more responsible standard of conduct.

variants.headline: A ship takes settlers away
variants.sub: People have left the colony on the ship: young adults without work and families without homes.
variants.body:
The colony has lost {left} people to departure on the ship in port. They include young adults with no work and families with no home. An assessment of {target} should address the practical conditions behind that leaving, rather than ask a movement of people to explain itself as a count alone.

Labour's question is not whether a person ought to love the colony enough to endure anything. Labour finds the stewardship of {target} wanting; ordinary people deserve a more responsible standard of conduct.
